chunks: Al-Hakim Abu Ali Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Bayhaqi narrated to us, saying: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sawli, saying: He narrated to us Abu Dhikwan, saying: I heard Ibrahim ibn Al-Abbas say:

I heard Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (peace be upon him) say: 'I swore by emancipation, and I do not swear by emancipation except that I free a slave. And after that, I freed all that I own, if he thinks that is better than this.' And he pointed to a black slave from among his servants, [saying]: 'Due to my closeness to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), unless I have a good deed, by which I would be superior to him.'

key_terms.بِالْعِتْقِ: by emancipation (swearing by freeing a slave)
key_terms.رَقَبَةً: a slave's neck (metonymy for a slave)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Imam al-Ridha's oath of emancipation and his view on superiority between nobility and righteous deeds?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (a.s.) employs the solemn oath of 'emancipation' to demonstrate that spiritual merit, derived from righteous deeds (amal salih), supersedes mere genealogical proximity to the Prophet (S). By pointing to a black slave, he illustrates that nobility is not inherent in lineage but is earned through piety, a key Shia concept distinguishing true superiority from social status. This incident, recorded in *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, serves as a critique of haughtiness and emphasizes the egalitarian nature of Islamic virtue.
